title: power-analysis result.json contract (merged GLS+PT-PX, SAIF flow)
description: Complete contract for <module>/Verification/power-analysis/result.json. On status=pass, stage_specific requires saif_artifacts + compile_info + failures + ppa_actual + requirements + power_by_scenario (compile_info carries vcs_version only). On status=fail, stage_specific.fail_reason is required (if/then below). ppa_actual / power_by_scenario carry PT averaged power_mw plus its three components; requirements[] is one verdict per requirements.json row this stage judges, and carrying it obliges ppa_actual with it (dependentRequired).

fix_owner.description: On status=fail: the rule that must act, named by this stage from what it read in the raw tool output. Deliberately NOT an enum — the derived input closure in rules.py is the only authority on which names are legal, and decide checks it there. Naming this stage itself (its in-stage remedy is exhausted) or naming nobody both mean a human decides.

compile_info.description: Identifies the tool that produced the activity, not the one that computed the power: PT prints its own version in the header of every power_flat.rpt these numbers were parsed from.

failures.description: Tooling/data failures (NOT a missed bound — that is a requirements[] entry with met=false).

category.description: What the parser itself detected, and only that: saif_dump = the SAIF came out empty; gls_uvm = that scenario's gate-level run reported a UVM error, or left no verdict beside its SAIF at all; ptpx_data = a PT-PX report is absent, missing its Total, or fails the Total = internal+switching+leakage reconciliation. Nothing else writes this array, so the enum is exactly the set of conditions the parser has a branch for. The upstream-naming values it used to carry (netlist/sdf/tb_uvm/gls_runtime/plan) encoded WHOSE artifact was at fault, which fix_owner now states directly; tooling named this stage's own environment, which the parser cannot detect and never wrote.

power_by_scenario.description: One row per scenario, all of them computed at the single LIB_DB the batch loaded: ptpx.tcl sets link_path once, outside its loop. So this is not a corner sweep, and corner_intent below is the plan's claim about the row rather than a property of the number beside it — the operating condition PT actually used is printed in the power_flat.rpt this row was parsed from.

saif_annotation_rate.description: Fraction of nets whose switching activity came from the SAIF, from switching_activity.rpt. Qualifies power_mw: the same number at 0.2 is mostly tool defaults, at 1.0 it is measured. null = not determinable from the report.

corner_intent.description: Carried through from the plan unchanged. Nothing in this flow selects a library per scenario, so two rows whose corner_intent differs and whose stimulus does not report the same power.

requirements.description: One entry per requirements.json row this stage judges: the script's verdict for a row with a target, the agent's (finalize --requirements) for the rest. finalize refuses an envelope that leaves any such row out, so a row nobody read cannot pass as silence.

actual.description: What was measured or observed, in whatever unit the row speaks.
